hypothesis: The E20-proven stable lower-body ONNX action subset supplies causal perturbation recovery while incompatible upper-body outputs are unnecessary for the locked standing product contract.

candidate_behavior.action_axis: mesh-component parent-bind axis from first policy

single_changed_variable: For policy-using variants, conditioned ONNX actions are masked to the lower-body family after raw inference; all locked product protocol parameters and evaluators remain unchanged.
validity_gates: Exactly three unique Normal and three unique ZeroActions repetitions plus one of each destructive control are present.
Every run is PRODUCT_RUN authority with the locked protocol hash and complete raw streams/render.
Normal uses nonzero lower-body policy actions; ZeroActions uses zero conditioned actions.
Target readback match ratio is at least 0.95 in Normal and ZeroActions.
DropControlDispatch fails for target_readback and ForcedSupportLoss fails for runtime_state or support_gap.
support_and_product_pass: All Normal repetitions pass every absolute criterion, destructive controls fail for their intended reasons, and median Normal recovery AUC is at most 80 percent of median ZeroActions recovery AUC.
falsification: Any Normal absolute failure, malformed control, or recovery AUC ratio above 0.8.
promotion_rule: A passing development-flag bundle justifies implementing the lower-body compatibility mask as explicit product behavior, followed by a second full bundle without the development flag. It does not itself change production defaults.
next: If the bundle passes, implement and test the product compatibility mask and rerun the complete bundle without experimental action-family arguments.
